take_homes: Start with one agent per recurring job and split only for different access, dialect or stance. Don't split to look thorough.
The synthesizer needs a framework to pick an answer, because without one it averages the views.
After every run, have the agent review the handoffs and write the lesson into the shared rules file. That file is something my team could use.

monday.move: Rerun the pilot-cohort brief with fresh data, using a crux file and a rules file, and send it to the pricing working group.

monday.stop_condition: The output contradicts a number in the Q2 review and I can't explain why.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, so everyone keeps their own copy.

misconception.why: Handing the synthesizer a strategy kernel changed the result more than any prompt wording. I still think prompts matter, but structure and shared files seem to matter more.

one_line: The split-or-don't tests and the handoff-rules file are worth the hour, but the page repeats 'one agent is the default' three times and gives you no way to check that the final briefing is true.
